newsitem.title: UK: UBS sees U.S. arbitrage in Hanson DAPS.
newsitem.headline: UBS sees U.S. arbitrage in Hanson DAPS.

text.p: Trading Demerger Advance Participation Securities (DAPS) in Hanson's four demerged companies got off to a slow start in London on Wednesday, but arbitrage-related activity is expected to pick up this afternoon when Wall Street opens, analysts said.

UBS, which began trading the DAPS this morning, said some arbitrage between DAPS on Hanson's Millennium Chemicals group and Hanson's underlying shares was seen, mainly because of a perceived misvaluation on Millennium.
DAPS in Millennium started at $29.37/$31.55, or an equivalent of 27p/29p.

"Some people feel Millennium is worth more than the UBS valuation ... so they're buying Millennium (DAPS) and selling Hanson shares," said UBS spokeswoman Claire Smith. "We expect to see more of that this afternoon from the U.S."
She declined to disclose figures on trading volume, but described business as steady.
UBS had valued Millennium at $27.24 to $32.68, or an equivalent of 27p to 29p per Hanson share, the DAP issue said.
One analyst, who asked not to be named, said the valuation on Millennium appears to be most out of line. He puts the value of the chemical group between 30p and 35p.

Arbitrage in the DAPS, which essentially allows investors to pick what part or parts of Hanson they want to own ahead of the demerger, set to begin on October 1, can be tricky since values on the DAPS are artificial, the analyst added.
The other problem is that investors cannot short the DAPS, a broker added.
"It's not a perfect hedge ... but if anyone is going to pick up on the "arb', it's going to be the Americans," he said.
Hanson is heavily traded in the U.S.
DAPS in the Energy Group started at 520p/540p, while DAPS in Imperial Tobacco began at 340p/360p.
DAPS in the new Hanson Plc, consisting mainly of building materials companies in the UK and U.S., started at 43p/45p.
UBS had valued Imperial between 36p and 41p, Energy Group at 67p and Hanson between 44p and 49p, the DAP issue said.
The DAPS can be swapped for shares as the demerger proceeds.

The shares in Millenium and Imperial are expected to start trading in New York and London, respectively in early October. However, the listing on the Energy Group is unlikely to start before the first quarter of 1997, UBS said.
